"Clean up" could mean several different things, and some of them would change a lot of files, so I'll start by looking at the repo without changing anything.

TOOL: git status --short && echo "---BRANCH---" && git branch --show-current && echo "---LOG---" && git log --oneline -n 10 && echo "---TREE---" && ls -la && echo "---UNTRACKED IGNORED---" && git status --ignored --short | head -n 50

Once I see the output, I'll list what I find (uncommitted changes, stray or generated files, dead code, config drift, and so on) and propose specific changes. I won't edit anything until you confirm which ones you want. If you already have something in mind, like removing unused files, tidying a directory, or fixing lint warnings, tell me and I'll narrow the scope to that.
